specification.problem: Equivalence checking of quantum states and circuits under several notions of equivalence (e.g., exact equality versus equality up to global phase). The abstract names these notions but gives no specific algorithm or equations.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Background definitions only, for a tiny instance: two n-qubit unitaries U and V given as circuits, checked for exact equivalence and equivalence up to global phase. The paper's actual algorithms, data structures, and scalability techniques for hundreds of qubits are outside scope and are not reconstructed.

symbols.meaning: pure n-qubit states as complex vectors

equations.label: Exact state equality
equations.abstract_quote: quantum states, which are represented by complex-valued vectors
equations.justification: States being complex vectors implies vector equality as the strictest equivalence notion; this is an inference.

equations.label: State equivalence up to global phase
equations.description: Physical equivalence ignoring global phase, for normalized states.
equations.justification: Standard fact; the abstract only says several notions of equivalence exist and does not specify this one.

equations.label: Exact circuit equivalence
equations.description: Circuits are equivalent when their unitaries are identical.
equations.justification: Standard definition of functional equivalence of circuits.
assumptions: Same qubit count and no ancillas or measurements

equations.label: Circuit equivalence up to global phase
equations.description: Equivalence ignoring an unobservable global phase.
equations.justification: Standard criterion via Cauchy-Schwarz equality in the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product.
assumptions: U and V unitary of the same dimension

registers.name: q
registers.role: data qubits on which U and V act

steps.description: Form the miter circuit V^\dagger U on n qubits for the two given circuits.
Test whether V^\dagger U is the identity exactly, or the identity up to a global phase.
For state equivalence, compare the output states exactly or up to global phase.

assumptions: The abstract gives no equations, so all equations are generic background or inference.
Only exact and global-phase notions are listed; the paper may define others (e.g., relative-phase or measurement-based equivalence).
The tiny instance is two n-qubit circuits with no ancillas.
